newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian shares plunge in kerb on Congress bombshell.
newsitem.headline: Indian shares plunge in kerb on Congress bombshell.

text.p: The Congress party's surprise withdrawal of support for India's minority coalition government drove shares sharply lower in off-market kerb deals across the country, brokers said on Sunday.
Shares of leading firms Reliance Industries and State Bank of India plunged by an average four percent in off-market deals in Bombay, New Delhi and Calcutta.
Analysts said panicky traders were unwinding positions after the Congress party's announcement that it was no longer backing Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda's ruling coalition.
They said it was unclear how Congress -- which has 142 deputies in the 545-member Lok Sabha or lower house -- would form a government.
"If Congress is taking a gamble on this one, it will be interesting to see how they will come out," said Rupa Bose, strategist at Paribas Capital Markets in Singapore.
Analysts said said prices were likely to fall sharply in official trade on Monday. Bombay's benchmark stocks index closed 72.05 points, or 1.9 percent lower, at 3663.53 on Friday.
"After this shocking and completely unanticipated news I wouldn't be surprised if we see a 200-300 point drop," said the head of trading at a foreign institutional investor.

Congress said it was formally staking a bid to form a new federal government. Deve Gowda said he will not resign but will face parliament when it reconvenes on April 21. The minority United Front alliance controls some 178 deputies.
"The first reaction will be that the market will of course go down," Bose said. "But if it goes down far enough I'll be calling a buying opportunity."
"This is something totally unexpected," said Ravi Gopalakrishan, head of sales at UBS Securities. "There's trouble ahead that doesn't look like it will be easily resolved."
Analysts said the Congress decision was bound to affect budget proposals, announced by the United Front last month.
"The budget proposals could fall flat on their face," said an analyst at a foreign institutional investor.

In the annual budget for 1997/98 (April-March), Finance Minister P. Chidambaram announced sweeping cuts in corporate and personal taxes. The proposals are scheduled to be passed by parliament once it reconvenes on April 21.
"Uncertainty over the budget which has yet to be passed mainly concerned the marketmen and triggered panic selling," said S.C Juneja of brokers Jaico Credit in New Delhi.
The head of sales at a foreign brokerage said the finance bill could be delayed in parliament.
"The Finance Bill has not been passed yet. If the government changes the new government can either accept this finance bill or put a new vote-on-account to tide over the next two to three months."
"The market will continue to head lower until there is some semblance of the shape of things to come," he said. "We are hoping there will be a swift end to this crisis."
